newsitem.title: USA: U.S. reports rise in airline deaths, major accidents.
newsitem.headline: U.S. reports rise in airline deaths, major accidents.

text.p: Airline passenger deaths and major accidents rose last year, although the fatal accident rate for commuter airlines alone fell sharply, the National Transportation Safety Board said Friday.

The board also said deaths and fatal accidents rates in general aviation, including private pleasure and corporate craft, fell to a 15-year low, but for-hire air taxis marked their highest rate in 15 years.
Overall, the board said preliminary data showed that 1,070 people lost their lives last year in 2,040 civil aviation accidents. In 1995, 962 people died in 2,175 accidents.
The board said in 1996, 380 people died in accidents involving U.S. carriers on scheduled and charter flights of planes with 30 or more seats and on large cargo planes.

Major accidents last year included the explosion of Trans World Airlines flight 800 off Long Island on July 17, killing all 230 people on board, and the crash of ValuJet flight 592 near Miami May 11, killing all 110 people on board.
The board, responsible for investigating aircraft accidents, said the 380 killed was the second highest number since it revised its statistical analysis data in 1982.
It said that in 1995, there were 168 people killed in large carrier accidents and 239 were killed in 1994.

The board said there were six major accidents last year, with a major accidents defined as meeting any of three criteria -- a large plane destroyed, multiple fatalities or one fatality with the plane substantially damaged.
It said that in the past 15 years, only two years had more major accidents. They were 1985 and 1989, with eight each. In 1995 there were three major accidents.
The board said the major accident rate in 1996 per million hours flown was 0.439, the fifth highest in the last 15 years.
It said that of the 380 people killed last year, 319 were passengers. The others were crew and civilians on the ground.
It said that based on passenger deaths, one passenger in 1.8 million was killed in 1996, up from one in 3.7 million in 1995 and about the same as in 1988 and 1989.
In additional to the TWA and ValuJet accidents last year, a total of 38 people were killed in two accidents involving non-scheduled cargo planes.

A Northern Air cargo plane crashed at Russian Mission, Alaska, July 20, killing all four people on board and on Oct. 22, a Millon Air cargo plane crashed in a residential area in Manta, Ecuador, killing four people on board and 30 civilians on the ground.
The board said scheduled commuter craft -- planes with fewer than 30 seats -- registered their lowest fatal accident rate in 15 years, to 0.032 deaths per 100,000 departures.
It said that although more people were killed in commuter accidents last year than in 1995, the accident rate fell because all were killed in a single accident.
In the accident, 14 people died in the runway collision of a commuter and a private plane Nov. 19 in Quincy, Illinois. In 1995, nine people were killed.

But the board said that on-demand taxis marked their highest fatal accident rate in 15 years -- 1.42 deaths per 100,000 flight hours. Last year, it said, there were 59 air taxi deaths, up from 52 in 1995.
